findings.description: The early-return shortcut returns max(max(0, self.min), self.max), but the original code computes max(max(0, self.min), min(result, self.max)). The shortcut is only equivalent if result >= self.max, which is the case here, so min(result, max) = max. When min > max both versions give min, so it matches. The real mismatch is the comparison threshold: exponent > log(max/multiplier) implies result > max, so the shortcut seems correct.
findings.rationale: Floating-point error in math.log could make the shortcut trigger when result is marginally below max, but the effect is negligible.
